Umbrella: #1263

## Problem

14 `scripts/check-*_test.sh` files (1,807 LoC, 39% of `scripts/` LoC) test the gate scripts' own bash logic. They run on every `make check` pre-push.

Refactor-adversary identified: gate self-tests are META-testing (the gate testing the code). They don't validate the code-under-review; they validate gate logic itself. Pre-push runs them on every commit — wasted cycles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [planned] AC1: extract `check-gates: $(addsuffix -test, $(GATES))` in Makefile.d/ci.mk
- [planned] AC2: remove gate self-tests from `make check` dependency
- [planned] AC3: add `make check-meta` target running all gate self-tests
- [planned] AC4: schedule `check-meta` in CI nightly (`.github/workflows/check-meta-nightly.yml`)
- [planned] AC5: pre-push `make check` time reduced ~30% (per adversary projection)
- [planned] AC6: gate-script edits trigger `check-meta` via path-filter (PR diff includes `scripts/check-*.sh`)
- [planned] AC7: document: "edit a gate? `make check-meta` validates the gate logic. Edit code? `make check` validates the code."

## Audit ref

Refactor-adversary "compounding refactors for the year" #3. Fewer skip-`make check` incidents like #1208/#1214 (cost ~25min/PR per `feedback_pre_commit_make_check`).

- [planned] AC4: update PR-body lint to NOT require scorecard
- [planned] AC5: document: "operator may include scorecard if useful; reviewer subagent provides equivalent adversarial check"

Deletion-adversary, post-PR-#1248 simplification audit. Pattern: load-bearing in April → killed (#906) → re-introduced June 9 as softer "fill out this table" mandate. Recurring re-bureaucratization to be permanently halted.

Umbrella: #1263

## Problem

4 gate scripts identified by deletion-adversary as 🔴 DELETE-NOW based on empirical "0 real fires in 90 days":

1. **Banned-phrase gate** (`scripts/doc-check.sh §banned-phrase`) — 11 hardcoded phrases (`blazing-fast`, `production-grade`, `seamless`, etc.). 0 merged PRs in 90d saved by gate. Workers don't generate marketing copy in 2026.
2. **TBD gate** (`scripts/check-tbd.sh`) — bare `TBD` placeholder ban. Last real fire = gate's own birth PR (#732). 3 escape-hatch syntaxes documented in CLAUDE.md = the gate causes more escape ceremony than prevents.
3. **PR-body close-keyword gate** (`scripts/check-pr-body-close-keywords.sh`) — `closes #N #M` vs `closes #N, closes #M`. Mechanical comma enforcement; `feedback_default_simpler` says "wait for the 5 PRs, not the lint".
4. **Comment-density gate** (`scripts/check-comment-density.sh` + test = 10.4KB) — 5% ceiling. Forces operator-escape via `<!-- comment-density-justified -->` HTML comment to dodge a gate complaining about comments. Comically self-referential. Reviewer-subagent lens 9 catches WHAT-narration far better than regex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [planned] AC1: verify each gate empirically — `git log --since='90 days ago' -G '<gate-name>'` count = 0 OR only gate-self-tightening commits
- [planned] AC2: delete `scripts/doc-check.sh §banned-phrase` block (keep doc-link checking)
- [planned] AC3: delete `scripts/check-tbd.sh` + `scripts/check-tbd_test.sh`
- [planned] AC4: delete `scripts/check-pr-body-close-keywords.sh` + test
- [planned] AC5: delete `scripts/check-comment-density.sh` + test
- [planned] AC6: remove invocations from `Makefile.d/{ci,lint}.mk`
- [planned] AC7: update CLAUDE.md — remove rule sections referencing deleted gates
- [planned] AC8: pr-lint-doc-check workflow stays (doc-link gate still needed) but no banned-phrase scan
- [planned] AC9: reversibility — single revert restores

## Total deletion

~13-14KB scripts + ~200 LoC CLAUDE.md ceremony

## Audit ref

Both 2-adversary audits agreed. Deletion-adversary called it: "deterrent theatre that pays cognitive tax on every push to defend against incidents that don't occur."

body:
## Umbrella

Tracks delivery of CI/gate simplification wedges identified via 2-adversary audit (deletion-angle + refactor-angle). Audit driven by empirical observation that PR #1248 cycle = 80.7min wall-clock, but CI itself = 8.9min (11%); remaining 89% is reviewer-loop + body-snapshot-lag empty-commit ritual.

**Authoritative source**: 2-adversary simplification audit (2026-06-10 session, post PR #1248 ship).

**Core findings**:
- 70 empty-commits to `main` w/ "refresh pr-lint snapshot" message (verified via `git log --grep`) — symptom of `feedback_pr_lint_body_snapshot_lag` workflow design defect
- 41 prod scripts + 14 paired tests = 4,638 LoC; 6 pr-lint YAML files = 441 LoC; 97 memory stub files
- Both adversaries converged on 5 gates that MUST stay (`make check`, `check-no-bare-sleep`, `check-doc-links`, `check-prompt-parity`, `check-reviewer-verdict` narrowed)
- Everything else is candidate for delete/demote/consolidate

**Honest savings projection** (per adversary consensus):
| PR class | Baseline | Post-Phase-1 | Post-Phase-2 | Post-Phase-3 |
|----------|----------|--------------|--------------|--------------|
| Docs PR like #1248 | 80.7min | ~20min (-75%) | ~12min (-85%) | ~10min (-88%) |
| Code PR (typical) | ~25min | ~22min | ~15min | ~12min |
| LoC + files deleted | 0 | ~600 LoC | ~1500 LoC + 97 files | ~1800 LoC + 97 files |

## Phase 1 — DELETE + NARROW (Week 1, priority:p0)

Highest ROI, lowest risk. Land FIRST.

- [ ] N1 (#NEXT) — narrow `check-reviewer-verdict.sh` classifier (drop docs/{specs,briefs,dispatch-templates}+CLAUDE.md)
- [ ] N2 (#NEXT) — live `gh pr view` body fetch in pr-lint workflows (kill body-snapshot-lag)
- [ ] DELETE 4 gates: TBD, close-keyword, comment-density, banned-phrase script
- [ ] DELETE A+ rubric scorecard MANDATE (keep optional, remove `feedback_grade_rubric` mandate)
- [ ] DEMOTE byte-equal-pin + phase-x-leak from CI to pre-push hints
- [ ] MOVE 14 gate self-tests from `make check` → `make check-meta` nightly

## Phase 2 — REFACTOR (Week 2, priority:p1)

Compounding wins. Land after Phase 1 settles.

- [ ] COLLAPSE pr-lint orchestrator → 1 matrix workflow (-360 LoC YAML)
- [ ] FLATTEN memory dir → 1 `docs/engineer/feedback-index.md` w/ anchor-per-slug (-97 files)
- [ ] EXTRACT `scripts/lib/pr-body.sh` shared lib (5× fewer `gh pr view` calls)
- [ ] CUT CLAUDE.md slug citation density by half

## Phase 3 — STRUCTURAL (Week 3, priority:p2)

Quality-of-life.

- [ ] CAP adversarial-review per `feedback_review_proportional` strict enforcement
- [ ] DISPATCH-TEMPLATE `_common.md` include directive
- [ ] audit-session COLLAPSE 9 phases → 1 w/ silent-pass sub-checks
- [ ] DEMOTE stale-TODO from CI shard → local pre-push hint

## What does NOT get touched (proven load-bearing)

- `check-no-bare-sleep.sh` — silent CI orphan-test class
- `check-doc-links.sh` — link rot from renames
- `check-prompt-parity.sh` — spawner↔dispatch drift
- `check-reviewer-verdict.sh` (NARROWED not deleted)
- 5 required-status-checks list (each maps to a distinct concern)
- CI shard boundaries (already optimal per setup-go cache sharing)
- Worktree management primitive (orchestrator owns it)
- `feedback_trap_projection` (compounded value 5× in 2026-06-04 session)

## Acceptance criteria

- [planned] AC1: Phase-1 slices ship in dependency order — N1 + N2 FIRST, deletions after
- [planned] AC2: each delete-slice verifies "0 fires in last 90d" empirically (git log + PR search) before merge
- [planned] AC3: Phase-2 starts only after 7-day green soak on Phase-1
- [planned] AC4: every deletion reversible by single revert commit
- [planned] AC5: track wall-clock per-PR-class pre/post each phase; abort if regression

## Out of scope

- Phase-X surfaces (multi-tenant, RBAC, billing, htmx UI rebuild)
- Unified Go gate binary (`regatta gate <name>`) — Phase-X cost > Phase-S benefit
- LLM-judge banned-phrase replacement — non-determinism + tokens
- Auto-gen rubric scorecard tooling — adds tooling for human-readable checklist
- `regatta review --pr N` orchestrator-level primitive — Phase-X-adjacent

## Surface
`[CI]` — Makefile.d/ + scripts/check-*.sh + workflows

## Finding
2026-06-10 operator feedback (live): "dev process so slow."

Empirical (lens 4 measurement + this-session observation):
- 31 `check-*.sh` scripts in `make check` (verified `ls scripts/check-*.sh | wc -l`).
- Local `make check` 5-10 min wall-clock; CI `verify-go` 8 min.
- Reviewer-verdict gate adds 5-10 min/PR per token paste + pr-lint snapshot refresh.
- 30% of dispatched implementer PRs hit gate failure post-push (recent: #1208, #1214, #1228).
- govulncheck on every PR adds flake risk (170-min outlier #1207). PR #1245 demotes.
- TDD-first 2-commit pattern doubles `make check` runs per PR.

Root: gate count grows monotonically; no retirement gate. `feedback_default_simpler` was the rule meant to stop this, but each new bug class trips the operator into shipping a new gate.

## Fix (smallest viable cut)

**Phase 1 — measure, don't lint**
1. `scripts/check-roi.sh` — for each `check-*.sh`, scan `git log --grep=<script-name>` + `gh issue list --search "<script-name>"` over last 60 days. Print (gate, last-caught-real-bug, count, caught/total-runs-ratio).
2. Run once, attach output to this issue.
3. Operator decision per gate: retire / keep / promote.

**Phase 2 — fast path for doc-only PRs**
1. `make check` learns `--diff` flag (already partial: check-tdd does this).
2. When the PR diff is markdown-only OR script-only OR workflow-only, skip Go test gates entirely.
3. Wire via Makefile target detection: `make check-fast` triggered by pre-push hook when no `*.go` files in `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`.

**Phase 3 — collapse 2-commit TDD into 1**
1. RED commit need only be ONE pkg test failure; allow `[TEST+FIX]` combined commit when ≤30 LoC.
2. Update `feedback_tdd_discipline` to allow squashed-TDD for trivial fixes; keep RED-first for behavior-load-bearing PRs.

**Phase 4 — gate retirement**
1. After Phase 1 ROI report, retire gates that caught zero bugs in 60 days.
2. Archive (not delete) to `scripts/archive/check-*.sh` with re-enable note.
3. Target: -5 gates from `make check`.

## Out of scope
- New gates (anti-pattern: response to slow dev = MORE gates).
- govulncheck retirement (PR #1245 in flight).
- Reviewer-verdict gate retirement (keeps an independent reviewer in the loop; cost-of-bypass too high).

## Acceptance
- Phase 1: `check-roi.sh` runs + report attached.
- Phase 2: `make check-fast` exists, skips Go test gates on no-`.go` diffs.
- Phase 3: `feedback_tdd_discipline` updated; squashed-TDD allowed ≤30 LoC.
- Phase 4: ≥3 gates retired with cited ROI evidence.

## Reopen trigger
60 days after Phase 4 lands; re-measure ROI.

## Related
- #1243 (PR-cycle stage measurement) — sibling.
- `feedback_default_simpler` (the rule meant to prevent this).
- `feedback_recognize_session_end` (also meant to prevent gate-proliferation).

## Surface
`[CI]` — `scripts/measure-pr-cycle.sh` (new)

## Finding
Adversarial-reviewed velocity audit — survivor H (cross-cutting, prereq for future cycle-time optimization).

Lens 4 reviewer flagged: every dev-velocity rec is speculative until per-stage PR cycle time is measured. Today we know wall-clock total (median 22.8min / p95 51min / max 170.5min over last 25 PRs) but not the breakdown: (created → first-check-complete) vs (first-check → all-green) vs (all-green → merged).

Without per-stage timing, future optimizations (pr-lint poll cadence, reviewer round-trip, CI shard balance) cannot be ranked.

## Fix
`scripts/measure-pr-cycle.sh <PR-LIMIT>` — one-shot, no daemon:
1. `gh pr list --state merged --limit <N> --json number,createdAt,mergedAt,statusCheckRollup,commits` for last N PRs.
2. For each PR, extract:
   - `created → first_check_started` (workflow trigger latency)
   - `first_check_started → all_checks_complete` (CI run time)
   - `all_checks_complete → mergedAt` (review + merge latency)
3. Print histogram per stage. JSON output for downstream analysis.

Run quarterly or on-demand when proposing a CI/dev workflow change. NOT a CI gate.

## Out of scope
- Daemon / dashboard / time-series storage (one-shot script only).
- Automatic regression alerts (premature per `feedback_default_simpler`).
- Per-author or per-label slicing (add when needed).

## Acceptance
- Script runs against last 25 merged PRs, prints 3-stage histogram + JSON.
- Documented in `docs/engineer/runbooks/measure-pr-cycle.md` (1-page).
- Cited by next dev-velocity dispatch as the prereq evidence collection step.

Next dev-velocity audit dispatch.

## Surface
`[CORE]` — operator-loop + prwatch + dashboard polling reduction

## Synthesis of 3 adversarial reviews on #1229 #1230 #1231

Three adversarial reviewers converged on the same conclusion: **ETag conditional-GET + smaller cadence/swap fixes win 80-95% of the polling-cost reduction at 5% of the engineering cost** — webhooks (#1229) and SSE (#1230) are over-engineered for single-operator self-host.

### Reviewer verdicts (one line each)

- #1229 webhook + smee.io → **REJECT-prefer-`gh pr checks --watch`** (`cavecrew-webhook-audit`). Operator session statelessness blows up the receiver model. `gh pr checks --watch` streams updates natively, no relay, no infra. The 27-min wall-clock in 2026-06-10 session is sequential batch processing, NOT poll cadence — webhook latency improvement doesn't address root cause.
- #1230 dashboard SSE → **REJECT-prefer-ETag** (`cavecrew-architect`). SSE adds reconnect / broadcaster state machine work. Real problem is full-panel re-render jitter, fixable w/ `hx-swap="outerHTML transition:true"` + `hx-preserve` (orthogonal to polling). ETag adds 304-on-unchanged = ~98% bandwidth reduction + zero connection-state.
- #1231 prwatch ETag → **APPROVE-with-amendments** (`cavecrew-adversarial`). Empirically sound. Amendments: explicit cache TTL + 200-fallback, agent-state-transition edge handling, 304+stale-snapshot test coverage. Note: **GraphQL bundle is a simpler alternative** (1 multi-PR query instead of N REST calls = 90% reduction, ~50 LoC, no cache).

Per `feedback_default_simpler`, ship ALL 3 as small targeted PRs:

**PR 1 (Ship-now S effort)** — `gh pr checks --watch` for operator skill CI poll

body:
## Problem

`internal/orchestrator/prwatch/prwatch.go::Sweep` runs every `TickInterval=5s` (orchestrator.go:109) and shells out to `gh pr list --head <branch>` (and a fallback `gh pr list --search title <prefix>` during a 12-tick rename grace) for EACH {running, pr_open} agent. At 4 active agents that is ~48 GH-API calls/min ≈ 2,880/hr per orchestrator instance — a hot path well inside the secondary-rate-limit guardrail.

The vast majority return the same `headRefOid` as the previous tick. Pure wasted I/O.

## Proposal

**Phase 1 — ETag + Conditional GET cache (small, ship now).**

1. Replace the unconditional `gh pr list --head <branch>` shell with a direct REST call:
   `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?head={o}:{branch}` carrying `If-None-Match: <last-etag>`.
2. In-process cache keyed by branch → `{etag, body-snapshot, observed-at}`.
3. On `304 Not Modified` (the common case): zero rate-limit cost, ~50ms round-trip, decode skipped, Sweep's reconciler walks the cached snapshot.
4. On `200`: refresh cache, run normal reconcile.

GitHub honors conditional GETs and charges 0 against the REST budget when 304 is returned.

**Phase 2 — Webhook-driven invalidation (defer; pairs with the operator-wake webhook infra).**

When the cross-cutting webhook ingress lands, `pull_request.{opened,synchronize,closed}` events invalidate the cache entry, forcing the next Sweep to re-fetch (200 path). Steady-state Sweep traffic drops to ~zero.

## Outcome

- Phase 1 alone: ~2,880 calls/hr → ~2,880 conditional-GET 304s/hr (zero quota cost, ~50ms each).
- Phase 2: ~2,880 calls/hr → ~10/hr (only on actual PR state change).
- No behavior change; pure quota + latency win.

## Effort

S (~30 LoC + tests, ~half-day).

## Adversarial

- *"Why not just slow `TickInterval`?"* — Slowing the tick delays new-PR detection. Conditional GET keeps detection latency at 5s without the quota cost.
- *"gh CLI doesn't expose ETag."* — Correct; this motivates bypassing `gh pr list` and using REST directly. PR-list call is the only shell-out replaced; rest of prwatch stays gh-CLI-driven.
- *"What about secondary rate-limit on the GET endpoint itself?"* — 304 responses still count toward the secondary limit's request-rate budget but not the primary 5,000/hr budget. Fall back to gh-shell path if the secondary limit ever fires.

## Citation

- `feedback_default_simpler` (CLAUDE.md) — smallest viable shift.
- prwatch.go:38-50 (current cadence comments).
- GitHub REST docs: conditional requests + ETag headers.

## Problem

Five dashboard panels in `internal/web/templates/layout.tmpl:38-90` use htmx `hx-trigger="load, every 5s"` (3 panels) and `every 10s` (2 panels) to full-refresh innerHTML. At a quiet hour this is ~45 HTTP round-trips/min per open dashboard tab — each one fully re-renders Go templates server-side even when the underlying state-DB rows are byte-identical.

Operator-visible symptoms:
- Screen jitter every 5s (panel content flashes, scroll jumps on swap).
- Wasted Go template-render CPU.
- Broken progressive-enhancement: the dashboard isn't usable without polling.

## Proposal

Replace per-panel htmx polling with **Server-Sent Events** via htmx's first-party SSE extension (~4kb, vendored alongside `htmx.min.js`).

1. Single endpoint `GET /ui/events/stream` (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`) — one long-lived connection per browser tab.
2. In-process broadcaster fans state-DB transitions out as SSE events: `event: panel-pipeline`, `event: panel-agents`, etc. Payload = the same HTML fragment the existing handlers return today.
3. Templates change shape from:
   ```html
   <div hx-get="/ui/panels/agents" hx-trigger="load, every 5s" hx-swap="innerHTML">
   ```
   to:
   ```html
   <div hx-ext="sse" sse-connect="/ui/events/stream" sse-swap="panel-agents">
   ```
4. Broadcaster sources: state-DB write seam (today's `state.Substrate.Append` path) — every write fans out a "which panels were affected" hint; broadcaster renders affected panels only.

## Outcome

- 45 req/min/tab → 1 long-lived conn/tab (~98% drop in HTTP overhead).
- Panels update on STATE CHANGE, not on timer — strict superset of current correctness.
- Empty-hint strings in `internal/web/dashboard.go:170-171` ("Scheduler ticks every 5s.", "Adapter polls every 30s.") get truthful when the underlying loops migrate.
- No external dependency; pure-internal refactor.
- htmx SSE ext is upstream-supported, no fork.

## Effort

M (~1-2 day spec → impl → roll). Risk: connection management at scale (irrelevant — single-tenant self-host); CSRF on SSE endpoint (handled like other endpoints).

## Adversarial

- *"htmx polling is already cheap enough."* — Disagreed; #1215 (htmx inline-style CSP violations + favicon 404) shows the dashboard is degraded silently; this work decisively replaces poll with push and clears the renderer-on-every-tick path that contributes load.
- *"SSE doesn't reconnect cleanly on flaky networks."* — htmx SSE ext has reconnect built in; on reconnect the broadcaster sends a `panel-full-refresh` payload as the welcome message.

## Citation

- `feedback_default_simpler` (CLAUDE.md) — simpler transport wins.
- Related: #1215 (htmx CSP violations).
- Reference impl: htmx SSE ext (https://htmx.org/extensions/server-sent-events/).

body:
## Problem

The regatta-operator skill's bounded-CI-poll pattern (`.claude/skills/regatta-operator/SKILL.md:455-484`) sleeps the operator session 60s/tick × up to 10 ticks × N PRs in a merge wave. Session 2026-06-10 burned ~27 min of operator wall-clock waiting for 4 PRs to clear CI. Same trap motivated MAX_TICKS=10 cap in session 5 (PRs #1183/#1184/#1185 sat BLOCKED while skill silently polled).

This is the highest-cost polling pattern in the repo by operator wall-clock.

## Proposal

Push transport for PR/CI state, hybrid push-notify-then-pull:

1. **smee.io relay** as the GitHub webhook ingress (no public host required; preserves single-tenant self-host).
2. **Local `webhookd` process** (or in-orchestrator HTTP handler) accepts deliveries on `pull_request`, `check_suite.completed`, `status`, `workflow_run.completed` events. Verifies HMAC signature with `X-Hub-Signature-256`.
3. **Event vocabulary**: emit `pr.mergeable.changed`, `pr.checks.terminal`, `pr.merged` on the state-DB event stream (or write a wake-file the skill polls cheaply).
4. **Skill rewrite**: replace bounded `until CLEAN; sleep 60` loop with `wait-for-event pr.<N>.terminal` (60s timeout × MAX_TICKS=10 stays as backstop, but normal path completes within seconds of CI finishing).

## Outcome

- Operator session sleeps 0s between merge waves on the happy path.
- Failure path: webhook delivers `conclusion=failure` → operator-side bottleneck-resolution loop fires within ~1s of CI completion (vs ~60s in current cadence).
- Same infrastructure unblocks prwatch/checks/adaptersync/merge prober polling (issues to be filed separately).

## Implementation sketch

- New package `internal/webhook/` with handler, signature verification, replay log.
- `cmd/regatta serve` gains `--webhook-listen` flag (default `localhost:9090`).
- smee.io setup documented in `docs/engineer/operator-runbook.md` (one-time).
- Skill subsection rewrites `.claude/skills/regatta-operator/SKILL.md` Bounded CI poll → Event-driven CI wake; bounded poll stays as fallback when smee.io unreachable.

## Effort

M (~2-3 day spec → impl → roll).

## Citation

- `feedback_bounded_ci_poll` (CLAUDE.md)
- Session retro 2026-06-10 (handoff at `.claude/session-handoffs/2026-06-10T16-49Z-session-handoff.md`)
- Issue precedent: #1192/#1193/#1194 (bounded-poll subsection bugs)

## Adversarial

- *"smee.io is an external dep"* — yes; offline fallback = current bounded poll. Failure-open is the simplest viable design (per `feedback_default_simpler`). Self-hosted alternative (own webhook ingress) deferred to Phase X.
- *"webhook delivery isn't 100% reliable"* — yes; webhook is push-NOTIFY, operator still pulls detail via `gh pr view`. Missed delivery degrades to next scheduled poll (degraded, not broken).
